newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czechs split on joining NATO - survey.
newsitem.headline: Czechs split on joining NATO - survey.

text.p: Czechs are split on the idea of becoming one of the first former Soviet Bloc countries to join NATO, an opinion poll released on Wednesday showed.

Of 1,001 people sampled, 38 percent supported the country joining the North Atlantic Treaty Organisation while 35 percent opposed it, the survey by the state-funded Institute for Public Opinion Research (IVVM) said.
The Czech Republic, along with Poland and Hungary, are widely seen as leading candidates for the western security alliance's planned expansion to former Warsaw Pact members.
The poll indicated 33 percent saw NATO membership as a guarantee of their country's security while 40 percent regarded the expected higher costs for the Czech army as the main disadvantage.
In October, U.S. President Bill Clinton called for the first batch of former East Bloc members to join NATO by the year 2000.
Czech politicians are mixed on whether there should be a national referendum on NATO membership.

The centre-right ruling coalition parties -- the Civic Democratic Party of Prime Minister Vaclav Klaus, the Civic Democratic Aliance and Christian Democratic Union -- are all against a referendum on the issue.
The strongest opposition party, the Social Democrats, support joining the alliance but are insisting on a plebiscite.
Two minor opposition parties, the Communists and the far-right Republicans are strongly against Czech membership in NATO.
